correctness.rationale: The pre-Schwarzian second derivative at each real strip point is exactly 6(a3-(2/3)a2^2), so the classical sharp Fekete-Szego bound gives |B''|<=6(1+2e^-4). Correct Gaussian centering yields phase error 3(1+2e^-4)sigma^2, while the exact oscillatory Gaussian factor and Cauchy-Schwarz give |Im G|<=4 sigma sqrt(sinh(sigma^-2)). With sigma=9/14 these bounds place the real-axis argument strictly inside a half-plane and give c0=6.4938486514e-4.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. arXiv:2609.20607v1 proves the universal metric comparison with an explicit lower constant about 1.29e-42 but does not use the Fekete-Szego functional or state this quantitative sharpening. Searches by source identifier, metric terminology, pre-Schwarzian/Fekete-Szego formulations, and the current SCOPE archive found no matching refinement. The source is extremely recent, so an unindexed parallel observation remains possible.

value.rationale: The result strengthens the newly introduced universal metric comparison by more than 5e38 in its explicit lower constant and identifies a structural bridge to a sharp classical coefficient theorem. It also repairs the local Taylor-centering and Gaussian second-moment slips in the source calculation while preserving the source theorem.
